spec_notes: The specification (docs/shiploop/spec.md) is a short list of checks and is silent on almost every unstated item in this share; the choices are recorded in README.md and the fix notes instead. Its 'Default:' lines mark three builder choices (one operator token for all personas; identity, type and readers not editable, value types preserved; a stopped server leaves tasks Interrupted for explicit retry). R-1 decides without marking it that Switch person clears the selection and reload keeps it. R-6/R-7 say UI-1 verifies controls, widths and keyboard and that npm test is the maintained verification, but npm test does not run UI-1 (browser.cjs registers no test under NODE_TEST_CONTEXT) and still reports it as passed. The spec does not contradict the request on these items.
tests_notes: TC-1, TC-3, TC-6 and TC-8 each cover several behaviours (selection, bots, restart; pending, failure, retry, dedupe; reading, clarify, reject, confirm-twice, conflict, readers, restart). Tied to internals: TC-14 parses index.html ids and data-limit attributes and forbids maxlength; TC-11, TC-12 and TC-20 test public/rules.js browser helpers directly; TC-16 renames the data folder and expects a log line with 'ENOENT'; TC-18 and TC-19 pin exact message wording; TC-22 pins the title/detail format. Timing-dependent: TC-8, TC-15 and TC-16 rely on STANDIN_STEP_MS values and short delays. Would fail on another correct build: TC-7 expects the previewed create object exactly {id:'ORD-1005', ..., readers:['maya']}; TC-3/TC-13 expect the action names, requestId field and reply.status shape of this API; TC-10 expects a 409 refusal where overwriting with a notice is also acceptable. test/browser.cjs is skipped silently by npm test.
maintainer: lib/workspace.js puts every action in one switch inside a single copy-on-write store.write transaction over one JSON snapshot, and the per-person boundary depends on locate() always starting from state.users[person.id]; a change to how bots, threads, proposals or tasks are looked up could open another person's data. In the browser, public/app.js's replace()-by-JSON-key rendering, focus restoration and the revision/polling interplay are intricate, so changing what a region shows risks stale views or lost focus without any npm test noticing.
